proof_summary: Set \(\epsilon=\tfrac12\) and choose an arbitrarily large prime \(p\); the only positive integers \(k\le p\) whose prime factors all lie among those of \(p\) are \(1\) and \(p\), so \(a(p)=2\). For sufficiently large \(p\) (explicitly, \(p\ge81\) suffices), \(\sqrt{\log p}>2\), contradicting the asserted eventual lower bound.
